text:
Rose, totally agree. 

Long post! Thx in advance for reading.

Homelessness is complex. 

I volunteered for a short time with a Christian urban ministry in CA. Dont want to give its name, ‘cause I dont speak for it. It is a faith-based organization. 

I don’t always know what my beliefs are, but their beliefs are v clear. Jesus walks with these people. ❤️

I went with the Ministry to Mississippi after Hurricane Katrina wrecked the Gulf coast. 

The Ministry went to Biloxi to hand out food and water and help the people recover. While I was there I met one of the Ministry’s homeless program’s “graduates,” Kraig. 

Kraig was a heroin addict for many years, living on the street in towns up and down the west coast. 

He ended up going to prison in Nevada. Told me he got sober and found Christ in prison, and connected with the Ministry when he got out. 

The info below is the process the Ministry uses to help homelessness. 

The process is extensive, but it’s probably what’s actually required to take a homeless person off the streets and get them into a permanently “stable” life. 

I challenge anyone to look at the process and see if any city in the US could provide this level of primary, continuing aid. 

Kraig said the average time in the Ministry of moving from homelessness to “permanent stability” was greater than two years.

Their process, as I understood it:

The Ministry takes a homeless man off of the street, and initially offers: 

A bed in a night shelter
A chance to shower, shave 
A change of clothes
A meal 
Immediate urgent medical care 
A 12-step meeting

The requirement: the man must follow rules in the shelter, including no drugs, drinking, violence or aggression.

Man is evaluated. If the man is willing, and accepted, he enters the long-term program. In the program, man is given: 

a shared long-term room
regular meals
access to shower 
hygiene supplies
new clothes
continuing urgent medical care
access to 12-step programs

The man is expected to follow the rules, attend faith-based services and classes, interact with a 12-step program, and contribute to the Ministry’s programs (e.g. prepare meals, counsel new members, clean the shelter, follow through on commitments.) No drugs or alcohol are allowed. No uncivil behavior. The man is held accountable. 

In return, the Ministry will also help the man:

get a legal ID 
find permanent housing 
reconnect with his family, if desired
complete a high school GED 
obtain a driver’s license 
receive long-term counseling 
continue in 12-step programs
find a job (the Ministry created a whole job center just for these men; they often work together in construction teams; make good money.) 
find education or training 
receive bilingual language training if needed

The Ministry has an equivalent program for women. 

The Ministry has an equivalent program for parents with minor children.

I don’t know the Ministry’s statistics - don’t know how many people enter the programs, how many “graduate”, how many go on to achieve long-term stability. I think the numbers are probably pretty good. I can’t imagine the costs involved. I believe the Ministry is nonprofit. 

Kraig entered the program as a homeless, recovering addict and felon. When I met him in Mississippi, he was training to become a Christian minister, was working full time in a good construction job, and was helping a mostly-black Christian  congregation in Biloxi put a new roof on their church. Kraig is a white man. Kraig is a good man. 

Homelessness is complex. It can be solved, but it requires long-term commitment and continuing investment over years in many areas of a person’s life. 

This is the kind of investment a family  makes in their members.

The Ministry is stepping into people’s lives and caring for them like family.

I think it’s very challenging for any city to try to take this on, even if given millions of dollars. 

In LA county, CA, alone, the estimate of homeless addicted people is something like 30,000.

Tulane Green Wave

Class of 2026 Spotlight

DE
 Jordyn Crites- @JordynCrites26 
6-7/274
Friendswood, TX
 Jordyn Crites is a towering defensive lineman from Friendswood High School in Friendswood, Texas, class of 2026. 
 Standing at 6-7 and weighing 274 pounds, Crites combines exceptional length with athleticism, making him a disruptive force on the edge or interior. 
 He signed with Tulane on December 3, 2025, after committing on June 14, 2025, choosing the Green Wave over 16 FBS offers, including Power 4 programs like Baylor, TCU, Oregon State, Texas Tech, and others such as Coastal Carolina, Louisiana, North Texas, Rice, San Diego State, Tulsa, UNLV, and UTEP.     
 Crites transferred to Friendswood after attending Edmond Memorial in Oklahoma for his freshman and sophomore years, where he began building his profile.   
 He also played tight end, showcasing versatility, but his future is on defense. 
 Crites was noted as a “riser” in recruiting circles.   
 His recruitment heated up with official visits to TCU, Tulane, and Baylor in June 2025.  Crites was praised for his potential as one of the top defensive linemen from Texas, with Power 4 interest. 
 Scouting Report:
 Frame and Length: 
Enormous wingspan and height make him a mismatch nightmare, allowing him to disrupt passing lanes and engulf ball carriers. His reach helps in shedding blocks and maintaining leverage.   
 Power and Hand Usage: 
Violent, heavy hands at the point of attack; primary move is a pure power rush that overwhelms offensive linemen. He can swim and dodge as counters, showing developing technique. 
 Athleticism and Bend: 
Exceptional bend for his size, allowing him to break down in the backfield and pursue with speed. His 4.8 40 and vertical translate to explosive get-off and closing burst. 
 Motor and Production: 
High-motor player who lives in the backfield, generating sacks, hurries, and numerous tackles for loss (TFLs). Effective against both run and pass, with a dynamic presence that wrecks games. 
 Versatility and Upside: 
Two-way experience (DE/TE), with unreal potential due to size, power, and athleticism. He’s come into his own recently, suggesting continued growth. 
 Intangibles: 
Strong academics, track background, and resilience shown in transferring schools.

text:
Podcast Summary | The Shawn Ryan Show: #334 Clint Emerson - Inside SEAL Team 6's Spy Unit: Black Squadron

Overview

Clint Emerson's path from an American childhood inside Saudi Arabia to the silent ranks of SEAL Team 6 is a study in the formation of a special operator. His early exposure to a strict, sometimes hostile, foreign culture instilled a specific drive, but it was a near-drowning as a child that became his psychological anchor for surviving the brutal crucible of BUD/S. This conversation spans the absurdity and danger of pre-9/11 SEAL life, from hazing rituals and training with killer dolphins to the grim, chaotic opening months of the Iraq War. The threads that bind these experiences are the unspoken codes of brotherhood, the persistent tension between enlisted operators and risk-averse leadership, and a deep-seated need to prove one's worth that never fully extinguishes, even after reaching the pinnacle of the special operations community. Emerson’s story is not just about combat; it is about the personal cost, dark humor, and profound trauma that forge a warrior’s identity.

Key Themes

- Childhood adversity, specifically a near-fatal scuba diving scare, becomes a deliberate psychological tool used to reframe the suffering of SEAL training as manageable.
- A lifetime of low-level hostility and cultural alienation in Saudi Arabia directly fueled Emerson's motivation to enlist and later deploy to the Middle East with a desire for retribution.
- An unyielding code of silence among operators is paramount; Emerson endured severe physical punishment rather than identify an instructor who caused a classmate's career-ending injury.
- The pre-9/11 SEAL teams were a paradox, operating with less tactical intensity but engaging in dangerous hazing and serving as training apparatuses for military dolphins.
- A perpetual conflict exists between enlisted men who seek to execute their mission and senior officers whose lack of combat experience and risk aversion hamstrings their effectiveness.
- Combat in the early Iraq War was characterized by chaos, unclear lines of engagement, and a stark contrast between the grimy reality of the line units and the well-equipped, surgical operations of higher-tier commands.
- The trauma of a broken home and the pressure of an uncelebrated stepfather drive a persistent need to prove one's worth that extends far beyond earning a Trident.

Detailed Summary

Emerson began his life in Texas before his father's work for ARAMCO relocated the family to Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia. He spent his formative years on a secure Western compound, an environment punctuated by anti-aircraft guns and razor wire. The Kingdom in the 1980s, as he recalls, was a radical Islamic state with a rigid social hierarchy. Westerners were second-class citizens, forced to yield at every queue and subject to harassment, with young Saudi men throwing hard leather sandals at him from distances that felt like being hit by a plate. The system was flush with oil money but morally contradictory; Coca-Cola was banned due to its purported Crusader symbolism, while visas required costly annual exits from the country.

The strict environment defined his worldview. He left the region because schools only went to eighth grade. The turning point came in a Frankfurt airport, where a chance encounter with a Navy SEAL—recounting a mission to neutralize anti-aircraft guns before a bombing run—changed his ambition from ninja to frogman. This was reinforced by a school aptitude test that matched him with underwater demolition. The final nudge was a literal life-or-death experience. At twelve, on his first open-water dive at Tire Reef in the Persian Gulf, he became separated from his group and panicked. After what felt like a lifetime of treading water, he kicked hard enough to spot land and swam back, an experience that later served as a touchstone: "I've already been lost at sea." BUD/S, he reasoned, could not be worse.

This psychological anchor proved vital. Emerson enlisted in the Navy despite being close to a college degree, hiding his decision until two weeks before boot camp. At BUD/S, as a student named Smith in Class 203, he was repeatedly blamed for the deficiencies of other Smiths, accumulating punishment chits and extra sessions with a "wired tight" instructor fresh from SEAL Team 6. During one session, the instructor kicked another trainee, Garcia, breaking his ankle. While the class pressured Emerson to name the instructor, he refused, enduring a "death march" and continuous beatings rather than violate the code. Years later, he ran into the same man, now a warrant officer, and revealed he had saved his career. The man admitted he had "almost got cam" for the incident, and they shared a laugh, a moment of closure for both.

His determination was rooted in a desire to return to Saudi Arabia and "mess with these people." He also sought to prove he was not a loser, a feeling born from his pre-Navy life. This drive to prove his worth persisted even after making it to a tier-one command. The conversation noted the common lore that most special operators come from broken homes; Emerson speculated that his own childhood trauma was a beacon for what could be overcome. The loss of his stepfather, who died suddenly of a heart attack right as he was finishing training at SEAL Team 3, added another layer of grief and motivation. His stepfather had volunteered to raise him, and Emerson wanted to share his SEAL stories with the man who truly earned them. This emotional weight was something he learned to compartmentalize, to "deep six it" and deal with it later.

Life at SEAL Team 3 pre-9/11 was its own distinct world. The culture was less intense than today's, characterized by liberty and hazing rituals that could turn dangerous. Emerson recounted his own "initiation," involving being stripped and taped with blasting machine leads attached, nearly thrown into a covered pool. Training was often ad-hoc. In one memorable exercise, his platoon chief, a former Marine, bear-hugged a pier pylon while Emerson lay on the sandy bottom, both using Draeger rebreathers to avoid Navy dolphins. These dolphins, equipped with harnesses and capable of killing a great white shark, "took turns punching" the chief. The primary job was to serve as training apparatus, with the famous dolphin Jake rumored to have broken several operators' bones before being retired and deployed to harbors worldwide.

The pre-9/11 operational focus was ship boarding in the Persian Gulf. Team 3 had become "the pros," inventing protocols to infiltrate behind tankers using radar shadows and scaling six-inch-wide caving ladders at 20 knots in rough seas to board vessels and hand them over to NATO forces. It was one of the few operational jobs available, making it a sought-after deployment. The world changed on 9/11, which Emerson watched unfold from the Team 3 quarterdeck after receiving a phone call while driving across the Coronado Bridge. The pace shifted from "ops of the decade" to "ops of the night." On the way into Iraq, morale was complicated. At a staging base in Kuwait, they built a "tent city" with mocking signs aimed at reserve officers seeking combat experience, which leadership tolerated to keep spirits up, followed by a "war garden."

The first major operation was a gas-oil platform, which the command decided to approach by loud jetboat rather than stealth. The intel suggested a handful of bad guys and a hostage, but they found dozens. The platform was 1 kilometer long, seven decks high, and wired to explode. The assault was chaotic, with a nervous boat crewman accidentally firing the first shot into an oil pipe. They cleared the structure, finding shoulder-fired weapons and explosives below the waterline, and ultimately killed 27 enemy fighters. Afterward, they drove north in unarmored Humvees into a war that defied expectations. They witnessed the grim reality of trench warfare and slept on medical waste covered in hypodermic needles. The team was ordered by Colonel Kelly, later General Kelly, to conduct "100 killer ops" against a city of 80,000 with just 16 men.

Their missions were often dark and covert. At night, they secretly pulled the bodies of dead Marines from front-line trenches to protect morale, attributing the deaths to "fedeyeen" throat-cutters, a rumor that gave Emerson nightmares. They engaged in hunter-killer missions against Scud sites and cleared buildings ahead of the line. The conflict was starkly different from the sanitized public perception, as they saw burned-out US tanks and convoys. At one point, the entire convoy fell asleep at sunrise near "Toree," forcing Emerson to wake dozens of vehicles to avoid being sitting ducks. From a distance, he witnessed the Jessica Lynch rescue, contrasting his grimy reality with the "Guccied out" SEAL Team Six operators who annihilated the target from their armored supercharged Humvees.

These experiences highlighted the tension between enlisted operators and their leadership. Emerson openly challenged Captain Harwood in a debrief, accusing him of hamstringing the team and preventing them from doing what they were trained to do. He saw the early war's ROE as dangerously ambiguous, where every male of fighting age was a potential threat. Despite being offered a path to become an officer, he threw the OCS package in the trash in front of his chief, choosing to remain enlisted, where he felt the true operators "ran the show." The enduring impression is that the spirit of the SEAL teams is carried by its enlisted men, who navigate the absurdity and trauma of war with a dark humor and a fierce, unbreakable loyalty to each other.

Avatar: The Last Airbender: The Official Book of Amigurumi is an official standalone crochet pattern book published by Insight Editions. This original collection expands the world of the animated series into the realm of crafting, taking makers on a deeper journey through the beloved characters and creatures of the Four Nations.

The craft book features more than 20 standalone crochet projects, bringing together iconic heroes, villains, spirits, and creatures through a shared celebration of creativity. Rather than following a single narrative arc, the collection offers handmade interpretations of characters from the beloved series, including members of Team Avatar, Uncle Iroh, and the Cabbage Merchant, alongside memorable creatures such as Appa and the Turtle Ducks.

The 144-page book is written by Lee Sartori who created most of the designs. Guest pattern designs include @chrisette_ , who designed the Turtle Duck and Monk Gyatso, and cozylittlemess on IG, who designed June and Nyla as part of the QR bonus content. The collaborative project also features full-color photography, clear step-by-step instructions, and essential stitch tutorials.

The collection brings the world of Avatar: The Last Airbender beyond the screen, allowing fans to crochet their way through the Four Nations. With projects ranging from beginner-friendly creations to more intermediate designs, the book offers makers the opportunity to bring their favorite benders, characters, and companion creatures to life.

Official News Release:
Junction City Council confirms employment offer to Benjamin West
08/27/26

The City Council for Junction City confirmed an employment offer to Ben West of Wilsonville, OR, to serve as Junction City’s next City Administrator. The Council also authorized the Mayor and Council President to negotiate an employment agreement with West for later adoption by the Council. The City Council made the initial offer on August 18, following a two-day interview process subject to completion of the background check. Council reviewed criminal history, civil litigation, verification of employment and education, and reference checks to address this matter.

One issue the Council reviewed in detail was an ethics complaint filed in May regarding Clackamas County's employment of Ben West’s father in a temporary position. By all accounts, Mr. West’s involvement leading to the complaint was an inquiry he made to the County Administrator about whether there were any job openings relating to his father’s skill set. There is no evidence that he had any further involvement in securing a job for his father. Mr. West attended an executive session to directly answer any questions the Council had about his background, specifically the ethics complaint. In consultation with Junction City’s legal counsel and the City Administrator Pro Tem, Council agreed that the nature of this complaint would not have an impact on his suitability to fill this position.

Mayor Ken Wells stated: “It is important for the Council to do due diligence to understand the background of Mr. West to ensure that he would be a good fit to fill the position of City Administrator. Following this review, the Council was comfortable with proceeding with negotiating an employment agreement with Ben.”

“I am genuinely eager to serve as the next City Administrator for Junction City and to become an integral part of this community,” stated West. “My enthusiasm runs deep, and I am confident we will work effectively together to address Junction City’s pressing issues.”

West is completing a four-year term as a County Commissioner in Clackamas County (pop. 421,000) and is a US Navy Reserve Lieutenant and Registered Nurse. Ben also served as City Councilor for Wilsonville from 2019 to 2022.

West has taken the lead role in working through a variety of hurdles that led to a $44 million Recovery Campus and transitional housing project for Clackamas County, which had groundbreaking ceremonies. He has worked closely with many officials and agencies in Oregon on various funding and policy issues for Clackamas County. In the Navy Reserves, he serves as a commissioned officer in a complex, mission-driven organization.

For further information, contact:
Spencer Nebel, City Administrator Pro Tem, snebel@ci.junction-city.or.us
Phone (541) 998-2153

text:
🏈 NOTRE DAME + G5

• Year two of CJ Carr. He already owns Notre Dame's passing efficiency record, and the offense now runs through him after losing the first two RBs drafted.
• Carr's next leap: pre-snap reads, pocket strength and playing calmer. His worst games came vs. USC, Texas A&M and Miami.
• Defense could be elite: four veteran CBs, two top recruits, both safeties back, full LB rotation and Oregon transfer T'Vondre Gray inside. 11-1 is the expectation.

🏈 G5
BOISE STATE
• The new Pac-12 has real depth — no easy weeks. Boise can't afford any sleepwalk games.
• Maddux Madsen's growth comes from tougher opponents. His struggles have come against Penn State, Notre Dame, USF and Washington.
• RB room may be the best in the G5. 10-2 likely gets playoff consideration; 9-3 probably misses.

FRESNO STATE
• Fresno ranked THIRD nationally in returning production from the portal. Players chose to stay despite bigger offers.
• Brian Ferentz takes over OL, and getting Roland Follywood back at RT solves a major roster concern.
• QB remains the biggest question. After last year's carousel, the cornerback room will decide the ceiling.

USF
• Brian Hartline brings a complete culture shift: CEO-style leadership after Golesh's offensive identity.
• Tim Beck installs a slower pro-style offense — the biggest question is whether it fits USF's tempo-driven success.
• Defense replaces nearly every star with transfers. Floor is around 7-5; ceiling is winning the American.

This goes back to the capture of science by Pharma, & of government by the corporate sector generally - including Pharma.

This has got little to do with objective science. I did a deep dive on this in a new book (1,600 citations).

Here's how ‘The Science’ is arrived at:

- 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲-𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿 (𝗻𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆).

(The few independent trials have a much lower success rate than the Pharma-funded ones. And they identify many times the side effects.)

- 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹𝘀’ '𝗮𝗿𝗺𝘀𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗴𝘁𝗵' ‘𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁’ 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗲𝘀 (𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗰𝘀, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴, 𝗲𝘁𝗰) 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝘆𝗽𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲-𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼𝗼.

- 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝗷𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀 𝗸𝗲𝗽𝘁 𝗮𝗳𝗹𝗼𝗮𝘁 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲-𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿 & 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿 𝗱𝗿𝘂𝗴 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝘃𝗶𝗮𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘁𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴.

- 𝗔𝗱𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗷𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀’ 𝗲𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀, 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗱𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆, 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 ‘𝗳𝗲𝗲𝘀’ 𝗯𝘆 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮.

(In 2014, each editor of 𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘈𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘊𝘰𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘨𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘊𝘢𝘳𝘥𝘪𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘺  received, on average, $475,072. Plus another $119,407 for ‘research’.)

Most stages in the lab-to-jab pipeline have this double layer of 'insurance'.

- 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗮 𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆. 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮, 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝘀.

(E.g. Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration gets 96% of its funding from the drug & vaccine industry.)

- 𝗦𝗼 𝗱𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀’ ‘𝗮𝗿𝗺𝘀𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗴𝘁𝗵’, ‘𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁’ 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗲𝘀. 𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲, 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻’𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗵𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗮𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰 𝗠𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘁 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽, ‘𝗮𝗻 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗲’ 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝘀 ‘𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲’ 𝗼𝗻 𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀. 𝗜𝘁𝘀 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆.

- 𝗜𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲 '𝘄𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗹𝘆', 𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗼 𝗱𝗼 𝘄𝗲𝗹𝗹—𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺 𝗼𝗳 𝗴𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮 𝗷𝗼𝗯𝘀𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘃𝗲.

- 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀—& 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗴𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘂𝘁—𝘁𝘆𝗽𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗲𝗻𝗷𝗼𝘆 𝗹𝗮𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗰𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗮, & 𝗮 𝗿𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀 & 𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗱 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀.

“𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒕𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕 𝒉𝒂𝒔 𝒃𝒆𝒆𝒏 𝒈𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒏 𝒃𝒚 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑴𝑯𝑹𝑨 [𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒓𝒆𝒈𝒖𝒍𝒂𝒕𝒐𝒓]—𝒘𝒉𝒐 𝒂𝒓𝒆 86% 𝒇𝒖𝒏𝒅𝒆𝒅 𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒎𝒔𝒆𝒍𝒗𝒆𝒔 𝒃𝒚 𝑩𝒊𝒈𝑷𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒎𝒂—𝒕𝒐 𝒂 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒑𝒂𝒏𝒚 𝒘𝒉𝒊𝒄𝒉 𝒊𝒔 𝒇𝒖𝒏𝒅𝒆𝒅 𝒃𝒚 𝑩𝒊𝒈 𝑷𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒎𝒂, 𝒕𝒐 𝒊𝒏𝒗𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒈𝒂𝒕𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒑𝒍𝒂𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒂𝒈𝒂𝒊𝒏𝒔𝒕 𝑩𝒊𝒈𝑷𝒉𝒂𝒓𝒎𝒂.”

In the book* I dub the impact of this long list of paid ‘voices’ 'the chorus effect'. The objective is 'end-to-end narrative containment'.

Most of the pipeline’s stages are shrouded in sepulchral secrecy. For example:

· 𝗪𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗸𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗣𝗳𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗿 𝗺𝗮𝗱𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗽𝘂𝘁 𝘂𝗽 𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗯𝗮𝗻𝗸 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗲𝘀, 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀 & 𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘆 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗴𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘀𝘁 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲 𝗲𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀.

· 𝗜𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗮 𝗹𝗮𝘄𝘀𝘂𝗶𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗣𝗳𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗿 𝘃𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗙𝗗𝗔 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗮 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗲—𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝘀𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵—𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝟮𝟬𝟵𝟳. (𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘀 𝗱𝗲𝗰𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗱, 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗯𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗻 ‘𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝗼𝗳 𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝗮𝗴𝗲’.)

The vaccine industry lives or dies by the chorus effect.

Its messages reach the public ear from a wide array of sources—expected & unexpected, central & marginal, official & unofficial—to create an impression of broad, & very diverse, support.

The 'chorus' is hired via a financial inducement to every player in the system—& even at its edges—from the one party with an overwhelming commercial interest in the outcome.

"𝑰 𝒅𝒐, 𝒚𝒆𝒔—𝒊𝒕'𝒔 𝒕𝒆𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒐𝒖𝒔𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒓𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈."

— 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗰𝗸, 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝗿𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗮𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗢𝗩𝗜𝗗 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗽𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗲—𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗳 𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝗱 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝗶𝗹𝘆𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗽𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗯𝗼𝗮𝗿𝗱.

Pharma can wait out RFK’s term—then pay off Congress to roll back his reforms.

Which means we need permanent political architecture to prevent this kind of system capture.

"NO ONE KNOWS HOW LONG THE SHORTAGE WILL LAST" - FULL $SKHY CEO INTERVIEW

SK Hynix CEO Kwak No-jung predicted that the memory semiconductor supply shortage will continue until the end of 2030, and that there will not be a sharp decline in demand thereafter.

Regarding plans for additional investment in the U.S., he reaffirmed the existing stance that investment is possible anywhere sufficient support is provided.

CEO Kwak gave this response to a question regarding how long he expects the memory supply shortage to continue during a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for an advanced packaging production base for AI memory at Purdue University’s Holloway Gymnasium in West Lafayette, Indiana, on the 27th (local time).

"No one knows how long the shortage will last, but there are no clear signs of a downturn," said CEO Kwak. "We expect the shortage to continue until the end of 2030."

He further explained, "I believe the next downturn will be different from the ones we have experienced over the past few decades. While adjusting production volumes appropriately is not easy, our business model for AI is transitioning from 100% standard products to partially customized or fully customized products."

In the case of AI memory, since it is custom-made for client systems, demand forecasting is easier and ties with manufacturers are stronger compared to the past. Consequently, the explanation is that even if a downturn occurs, the damage will not be as severe as in the past."

Even if a downturn hits, I believe demand will slow down slightly or remain at a stable level rather than plummeting," CEO Kwak said. "Therefore, I am not concerned about the period after 2030. I believe supply and demand will balance out, and the entire AI industry will grow together."

When asked about plans to invest in additional semiconductor production facilities in the U.S., he replied, "We are open to any location where sufficient resources, such as water, electricity, talent, and subsidies, are provided," adding, "Since nothing has been finalized yet, I cannot discuss specific details or directions."

Last month, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won stated, "If there is a suitable place, it does not matter whether it is the United States or anywhere in the world," expressing the same position.

However, CEO Kwak specifically added, "I hope to be able to deliver good news to the U.S. AI industry next time."

When asked if he felt pressured by the Donald Trump administration's demand for investment in memory semiconductor front-end process facilities, he replied, "Our current situation is very well known through media reports."

He reiterated, "We are reviewing any location in the world as long as it offers customers and new business opportunities," adding, "If the conditions presented by the other party are met, we would like to deliver another piece of good news to the AI industry in the U.S. or other countries, just like at today's event."

Regarding whether to continue maintaining its stake in the Japanese NAND flash company Kioxia (formerly Toshiba Memory), he answered, "There are no concrete or confirmed plans yet."

He further explained, "However, just as we contribute to the U.S. AI industry, we also intend to contribute to the Japanese semiconductor industry. Since we are investing in Japan just as we have in the U.S., we view it as our responsibility in some respects to contribute to that local community and the nation. Although there are no confirmed plans, we are carefully examining how we can grow the market together."

The clock is ticking on the chances to stop JD Vance
By Jonathan S. Tobin
When the Republican Jewish Coalition gathers this week in Las Vegas for its annual conference, it will honor the legacy of the late South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham and hear from many other prominent figures in the pro-Israel community. Doubtless, the proceedings will include the usual celebration of the U.S.-Israel alliance and President Donald Trump’s historic support for the Jewish state and his opposition to Iran and its Islamist terror network.
Equally, if not more important, will be an effort to sound the alarm about the hijacking of the Democratic Party by its intersectional and antisemitic left-wing led by the Democratic Socialists of America, or DSA.

That’s exactly what the RJC should be talking about. But participants should also be aware that along with the merits of the current administration and the threat that the Democrats’ increasing assumption of a position as America’s anti-Israel party poses, there’s another just as troubling peril hanging over their party and the country. And his name is Vice President JD Vance.

A big tent that includes groypers

Shortly before the convention began, it was announced that Vance will be addressing the RJC this weekend. That makes sense for him since it is a prime venue for potential candidates for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination. But the question hanging over his appearance will not be whether he utters the usual platitudes aimed at pleasing Jewish donors and voters. It will be whether he reverses course on some of the most important stands he’s taken in the past year.

Vance has assumed the role of the leading Israel-basher in the Trump administration, and whether he admits it or not, the advocate for a rerun of President Barack Obama’s disastrous appeasement of the nuclear threat posed by the Islamist regime in Iran. In and of itself, that would be enough to mark him as an outlier in an otherwise overwhelmingly pro-Israel Republican Party.

But the even greater concern about Vance is his belief that a “big tent” philosophy that seeks to include all who might conceivably support the GOP. Unfortunately, in Vance’s view, that includes its antisemitic groyper wing.

We got a reminder of this with the informal start of his 2028 campaign last week with a fundraising event in New York’s swanky Hamptons, where he raised a reported $5 million for the Republican National Committee. He has yet to declare his intentions, and the money will go to the party, rather than to a putative Vance campaign. Still, it’s clear that the vice president is using his side hustle as the RNC’s finance chair to get cozy with the party’s top donors, who paid $100,000 a piece to attend the reception and $250,000 for a seat at the dinner.

That’s political business as usual.

But what didn’t escape notice was that the event in the mega-wealthy beachside village of Southampton on the East End of Long Island, N.Y. was held at the home of Omeed Malik, the venture capitalist who heads the 1789 Capital firm among other lucrative holdings. Those sorts of credentials and a net worth estimated at $100 million don’t make Malik anything all that special in that kind of neighborhood. The reason his name may ring a bell is that 1789 Capital, a company in which Donald Trump Jr. is also partner, was the entity that invested the seed money in the amount of $15 million to help establish the Tucker Carlson Network. Malik and Don Jr. are reportedly close friends of Tucker. The same is also true of the vice president.

While no one should be held accountable for the bad behavior of their friends, the Vance-Carlson connection is more than personal.

The Tucker Carlson connection

It was Carlson, along with the president’s namesake, who is believed to have played the decisive role in persuading the elder Trump to help jumpstart Vance’s political career by endorsing him in a tightly contested Republican senatorial primary in Ohio in 2022. And the pair of buddies came through again for him two years later, when Trump tapped Vance to be his running mate in 2024.

The vice president has made it clear that he will always stick with his friends no matter what. As a general principle, that’s an admirable sentiment. But in this case, it involves him being willing to tolerate and tacitly encourage Carlson’s descent down a rabbit hole of antisemitism and obsessive hate for Israel, not to mention a bizarre affinity for the Islamist regime in Qatar—its Iranian ally—and Vladimir Putin’s regime in Russia.

In 2022, Carlson was still widely considered a tribune of modern conservatism due to his use of his influential perch as the host of a prime-time show on Fox News, where he led the opposition to wokeism, the “mostly peaceful” Black Lives Matter riots in 2020, and the authoritarian and ultimately futile COVID-19 pandemic policies of the Biden administration.

By 2023, however, his penchant for promoting conspiracy theories and an increasingly hostile relationship with the Murdoch family that owns the network, along with racist text messages that were made public due to the lawsuit against the channel about claims of voter fraud in the 2020 presidential election, led to Carlson’s firing.

Since then—and with the help of Malik and Trump Jr.—Carlson’s podcast has become one of the most watched and listened to political programs on the Internet, claiming nearly 4 million subscribers and tens of millions of views every week. But rather than merely continuing to express the same views he aired on Fox, which could be described as, for the most part, those of a mainstream conservative, he blazed a new trail on his own network. I had noted as early as July 2019 and then again in March 2021 that Carlson was a threat to the U.S.-Israel alliance and American Jews.

Those warnings were vindicated by what happened once the guardrails imposed on him by his bosses at Fox were removed. Since it was launched in December 2023, his podcast has become a regular source of openly antisemitic material. He has hosted and granted friendly interviews to Holocaust denier Daryl Cooper and neo-Nazi groyper Nick Fuentes. Every possible variety of Israel-basher, ranging from those on the far right to those on the left, has also been granted access to his popular platform. Along with them, a wide variety of preposterous anti-Jewish conspiracy theories—claiming that Jews invented pornography to subvert American society to bogus assertions about Jeffrey Epstein being a Mossad agent and the Chabad religious movement being responsible for the war on Iran—have been aired and endorsed on his program.

What’s more, the popularity of his show—at least in terms of Internet clicks, whether they are the work of real people or bots—has encouraged others on the right to join Carlson in venting animus at Israel and Jews, such as podcaster Megyn Kelly, not to mention even more extreme figures like Fuentes and conspiracy theorist Candace Owens.

Left-wing Jew-hatred has gained increasing influence over the Democratic Party and now threatens to dominate it as the DSA movement of Marxists and Islamists win primary after primary. But while the groyper wing of the GOP has flopped in the 2026 primaries, there is no denying that Carlson has become one of the most dangerous antisemites in American history.

That makes his close connection to Vance a significant concern.

What drives the ‘woke right’

Operating by the conventional rules of presidential politics, a potential 2028 contender like Vance would have ditched Carlson long ago, notwithstanding the favors he owes him. But that hasn’t happened.

More than that, when offered a perfect opportunity to establish a firewall between himself and Carlson last December at the Turning Point USA AmericaFest, Vance didn’t just pass on it. In his speech at the event, he did more than declare his neutrality in the argument between Ben Shapiro and Carlson about the latter’s antisemitism, both of whom also addressed the same forum. He said his vision of the Republican Party obliged him not to turn his back on Carlson and those who subscribed to his hateful stands, whether or not he agreed with them.

Vance had sung a very different tune during both his 2022 Senate run and the 2024 race, when he did well as Trump’s running mate (especially when compared to Democratic vice-presidential nominee Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz). In an address to the anti-Israel Quincy Institute, he made a case for the importance of the U.S.-Israel relationship as the ideal “America First” alliance because of the threat from Iran and other Islamists, as well as the fact that, unlike the Europeans, Israel is always prepared to fight for itself and alongside the United States. Since then, whether due to the influence of Carlson or not, he seems to have extended his neo-isolationist philosophy to ties with Israel.

Contrary to the brickbats thrown at him by his detractors, the vice president is neither shallow nor uninformed. He’s a genuine intellectual who, unlike many in the party establishment, moved from a stand in favor of pure free-market conservatism and hostility to Trump to one that rightly espoused a more common-good philosophy. Like Trump, he came to understand the way the Bush-era GOP had failed America’s working class. His critique of the European Union and its anti-democratic tendencies delivered in a speech in Munich in February 2025 may have scared globalist elites, but they were very much on target and in keeping with American values.

Yet his tolerance for the groypers—indeed, his seeming belief that they are an essential part of the Republican coalition if it is to preserve the gains it made under Trump once he leaves the stage in 2028—isn’t just wrongheaded. It is a reflection of a desire among some on the right to treat the post-Oct. 7, 2023 surge of antisemitism as something to be tolerated and even exploited, rather than to be condemned and tossed out of the party as Trump has done with Carlson.

The so-called “woke right” is merely a variation on the same theme of Jew-hatred that has become the new orthodoxy on the left. But it has far fewer adherents than those turning out to decide Democratic primaries in favor of candidates like New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Michigan Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, and many other DSA members and “progressives.” But if someone like Vance, who is unwilling to draw a line in the sand between them and the party of Lincoln and Reagan, becomes its leader, that distinction will no longer be of any importance.

Unless and until Vance reverses his stand on Carlson and a big GOP tent that includes the groypers, his 2028 presidential ambitions must be regarded as a genuine threat not just to American Jews and the alliance with Israel, but to the values of Western civilization that are the foundation of American democracy.

The 2028 GOP lineup

There are some obvious alternatives to Vance for Republicans.

Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), the runner-up to Trump in 2016, has made no secret of the fact that he still wants to be president. He’s also eager to make it clear that no consensus has been reached about the inevitability of Vance, despite the fact that the vice president has a big lead in far-too-early polls measuring the popularity of the 2028 GOP contenders. Moreover, Cruz has taken up the cause of fighting the growth of antisemitism with the sort of dedication and fervor few leading politicians have shown in recent years. But lingering doubts about his personal appeal and hold on the affection of Trump loyalists mark him as a longshot to win the nomination.

The most logical and potentially successful option for those who want to stop Vance is U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The competence and eloquence the former Florida senator has demonstrated as Trump’s second-term foreign-policy chief show how he has grown as a leader since his first disastrous run for president in 2016. And, like Cruz, his geopolitical views and consistent opposition to any hint of Jew-hatred make him especially appealing when compared to Vance’s affinity for Carlson and the groypers.

We don’t know whether he considers his pledge not to challenge Vance for president to be binding. If he doesn’t run—and if Trump doesn’t intervene in the contest to determine his successor—then, for the moment, the odds are that the vice president will win the nomination.

That ought to scare more than the people who attend the RJC event in Las Vegas. The prospect of a 2028 presidential race pitting an ally of the “woke right” against a representative of the antisemitic wing of the Democratic Party and the DSA like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) or some other Israel-hating progressive is a daunting one for everyone who understands the stakes for all Americans of such a dismal choice.

Of course, Vance will have the chance to allay concerns about him when he addresses the RJC. But unless he’s willing to explicitly reverse course on his TPUSA stance of neutrality on welcoming antisemites like his friend Carlson and others into the conservative movement and scale back his attacks on Israel, his speech ought to fall on deaf ears.

Pro-Israel Democrats may have already lost the battle for their party’s soul. Republicans who want to avoid that dilemma should be getting to work now to coalesce behind an alternative to Vance, not to mention doing everything possible to persuade Rubio to save his party and the country, and join the race. If they don’t, they’ll find themselves not just politically homeless in two years, but facing the likelihood of the election of someone comfortable with antisemitism being sworn into the presidency in January 2029.

Flash News 1
Hao Hong: Tech stock adjustment window may last until late August, but likely double-digit short-term rebounds

On July 30, during today's Binance Private Event, renowned economist Hao Hong stated that the major adjustment window previously forecasted by his team has opened and is expected to last until around the end of August. While there may be double-digit rebounds in the short term, the market remains in a deleveraging phase, and investors can afford to be more patient.

Hong pointed out that the South Korean KOSPI index has pulled back significantly from its highs, and the market is entering a phase where "bulls buy the dips while bears cut losses and exit." Because index weightings are highly concentrated in a few tech giants, their fundamental performance will remain the key factor in determining whether the market has truly bottomed out.

Regarding whether to position in tech stocks immediately, Hong indicated that bottoming signals are expected to become clearer over the next two to three weeks, making patience crucial in the interim. He cautioned that typical asset bubble bursts often undergo adjustments of two-thirds or even more; although the market has already dropped by about 50%, further downside cannot be ruled out.

At the same time, Hong noted that beyond price action, investors need to monitor factors such as South Korean regulatory policy, the deleveraging process, and foreign leveraged ETFs. He added that if this round of adjustment completes relatively quickly, it will offer long-term investors more attractive entry opportunities for these assets.

Europe is being invaded right now, enabled by criminal politicians across the continent. Illegal and uncontrolled immigration, driven by hypocritical political agendas and funded by taxpayers, is threatening Western civilization.

The same politicians who speak eloquently about multiculturalism and increasing immigration are often the same ones who send their own children to private schools where immigrants are absent. They also choose to live in the safest and most exclusive neighborhoods.

Understanding what is happening first requires pulling your head out of the sand. It requires admitting there is a real possibility that you've been spoon-fed bulls*it for years and, perhaps, conditioned to stop thinking critically for yourself. Many people simply cannot see what is unfolding.

The underlying mechanism behind the decline of many European countries, including Germany, the UK, France, Spain, Italy, Sweden, and Finland, is what @GadSaad calls suicidal empathy.

Gad Saad, a Lebanese-Canadian Jewish professor who recently decided to leave Canada, explains this concept in his latest book, Suicidal Empathy. The book is grounded in historical examples, scientific literature, and empirical research. It offers a framework for understanding what is currently happening across the West.

Why am I sharing this?

Because I care.

I care about Western civilization and its culture. I believe they are worth preserving. This affects every company, founder, leader, and employee operating in Western societies. Businesses do not exist in a vacuum. They are products of the societies around them.

More importantly, this affects the security and well-being of our families and loved ones throughout Europe. Western civilization is currently under attack, enabled by politicians who often show greater concern for criminals and immigrants than for their own citizens.

So do yourself a favor. Read Suicidal Empathy, or listen to it for free on Spotify. Pay attention to the emotions it stirs in you. Then ask yourself honestly whether there is a chance you've been misled for a long time. Ask yourself whether your family's future could be endangered by today's political decisions.

I've lived in many countries. I was born in Finland and am currently an immigrant in Paraguay, where I am doing my best to integrate into society.

I also spent five months during the winter of 2025 in Morocco and got a glimpse of the local culture and conversations. Many North Africans aspire to move to Europe, not necessarily to integrate but to benefit from the welfare system and "other opportunities". Many, not all.

Unless European countries fundamentally change their immigration policies, I don't believe the countries people are leaving will have strong incentives to solve many of their own underlying problems. At the same time, Western countries continue sending hundreds of billions abroad. Can you believe that!? Future generations will study this period as one of the defining political failures of our era.

Every European country should leave the EU. The sooner, the better. Public opinion is shifting finally, too. For example, in France, fewer than half of respondents now say the country should remain in the EU. That alone signals a major change.

Finally, if you want to understand what is happening in the world, X is currently the most valuable information platform. Traditional media has become heavily censored and increasingly promotes ideological & political narratives that discourage independent thinking. On X you can find all sides and learn to think for yourself again.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
Per @TheSteinLine, the Chicago Bulls are showing interest in restricted free agent Bennedict Mathurin.

The Los Angeles Clippers acquired Mathurin at the trade deadline in a deal that sent Ivica Zubac to the Indiana Pacers. While the Clippers would prefer to retain the 24-year-old  wing, they are reportedly open to listening to sign-and-trade offers.

Chicago is aiming to bounce back after a 31-51 season, with their rebuild centred around No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson. The Bulls have already been active this offseason, trading for Nic Claxton, re-signing Zach Collins, and adding All-Star guard Norman Powell.

Mathurin is coming off a season in which he averaged 17.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2.4 assists across 54 games. His scoring ability would provide a significant boost to Chicago’s second unit, while also addressing the team’s need for additional perimeter scoring.

Should the Bulls make a move and get this deal done?

text:
Former Brigham Young University football standout Curtis Brown and his wife, Kim, are mourning the devastating loss of their 2-year-old son, Haze, who died in a drowning accident at the family’s home.

Authorities said the toddler drowned on July 26, 2026 in the family’s private swimming pool in Clovis, California. Haze, who was described by loved ones as the couple’s “miracle baby,” was found unresponsive in the water by a family member, who immediately called 911.

Emergency responders, including police officers, firefighters, and medical personnel, rushed to the home. CPR was performed on the child, but first responders were unable to revive him. Haze was transported to a nearby hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

Police said there was no indication of foul play and the incident appeared to be a tragic accident.

A GoFundMe campaign created to support the Brown family described their loss as “unimaginable” and said friends, family, and supporters have come together to help them through the difficult time.

“Kim and Curtis recently lost their miracle baby, Haze, in a tragic drowning accident,” the fundraiser stated. “No words can ease the heartbreak they are facing as they grieve the loss of their precious son.”

The fundraiser’s organizer, Chandler Pearson, said it was created after people close to the family began asking how they could offer support. Donations are intended to help cover funeral expenses and other unexpected costs, allowing the family to focus on grieving and being together.

As of Wednesday, the fundraiser had raised more than $71,000 toward its $100,000 goal.

Pearson also encouraged those who are unable to contribute financially to continue supporting the family through messages, prayers, and by sharing the fundraiser.

Clovis Police Department spokesperson Ty Wood called the situation “an extremely unfortunate situation” and reminded families about the importance of pool safety.

“Adults should never let children swim unsupervised and should always learn CPR and keep safety and rescue equipment nearby,” Wood said.

Brown is considered one of the greatest running backs in BYU football history. He played for the Cougars from 2002 through 2006 and finished his college career with 3,218 rushing yards, becoming the school’s all-time leading rusher at the time.

He earned first-team All-Mountain West Conference honors in 2005 and 2006 after recording back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons. In 2005, Brown rushed for 1,123 yards and added 454 receiving yards, earning conference offensive player of the week honors twice. The following season, he rushed for another 1,010 yards while playing alongside quarterback John Beck.

His BYU rushing record was later surpassed by Harvey Unga in 2009.

After college, Brown signed with the Cincinnati Bengals as an undrafted free agent in 2007 and played in all four preseason games before being released before the regular season began.

Brown and his wife are parents to five children: Haze, triplets Cruze, Julie, and Kash, and their son Trey.

At the moment, the family has not publicly commented on the loss of their son.

text:
BYU FOOTBALL PLAYER CHARGED: BYU football player Matthew Ephraim Luapo Asiata has been charged following a July traffic stop in Provo that led to allegations of DUI and several other offenses.

According to charging documents, a Utah County deputy stopped Asiata after allegedly seeing him drive into a bike lane and block a sidewalk while entering traffic.

Investigators say they smelled alcohol coming from the vehicle and observed signs of impairment. Court documents allege officers found an open container of alcohol in the driver's door, and Asiata later admitted using a fake California driver's license to purchase alcohol while underage.

Prosecutors have charged Asiata with:

DUI, first offense
Using false identification to purchase alcohol
Minor in possession/consumption of alcohol
Open container in a vehicle
Providing false information to a peace officer
Driving without ever obtaining a driver's license
A lane travel violation

Charging documents also state Asiata refused a chemical test at the jail before investigators obtained a warrant for blood and urine samples. A preliminary urine test was positive for alcohol and THC, while blood test results were still pending.

Asiata's name may be familiar to many Utahns. In 2022, he survived a shooting outside Hunter High School that killed two other teenagers. At the time, his family described him as "a miracle" after he recovered from critical injuries.

text:
In 1972 a couple in Tonga sold their pigs and their chickens.
​
They had just finished a two-year mission. They had a houseful of children and no idea how they would ever pay to educate them.
​
The wife's sister had gone to America first. She lived with a family in Utah, graduated from the University of Utah, and took a job at U.S. Immigration. She helped with the papers.
​
So they came to Salt Lake City. The father had never seen a football game in his life.
​
All six of their sons would go on to play college football.
​
The oldest was eight years old when he landed. South High School, then Dixie College, then BYU, where he redshirted on the 1985 team.
​
Philadelphia drafted him in the twelfth round in 1988. Three hundred nineteenth overall.
​
One brother followed him to Dixie and then to Provo, played defensive end on the team that beat defending national champion Miami, and later wrote a book about it.
​
Another brother went to Utah. So did a cousin, who had wanted BYU and never got the offer.
​
The oldest came home and coached. Utah first. Then BYU's defensive line, where he was one of the only Tongans coaching Division I football in America.
​
He is a large part of the reason a generation of Polynesian players ended up in Provo.
​
He had met his wife back when he was a player and she was a Cougarette. She would later be elected mayor of Provo.
​
They raised five children and would not let a single one of them put on full pads until the eighth grade. They made them practice piano.
​
All five played college sports.
​
By 2018 there were four of them on BYU's roster at the same time. Two were his sons. Two belonged to the brother who had played at Utah.
​
Somebody once asked him about the family name and the weight it carries.
​
"They have a responsibility to live up to the name," he said. "I don't mean the football. Just the name they've been given, which represents many."
​
Fifty-four years after the pigs and the chickens, there is a junior on the North Shore of Oahu, at Kahuku High School, holding eight offers with more on the way.
​
BYU is one of them.
​
His parents are Victor and Moniqueca. Victor is the old coach's cousin.
​
His name is Puleivai. Everybody calls him Ace.
​
Kaufusi.
​
Now you see the whole picture.
​

text:
His father would not let him play football.
​
The man had played offensive line at BYU and in the NFL. He knew what the sport does to a body, and meant to make his son wait until high school.
​
The boy talked him down to sixth grade, because all his friends were playing.
​
He was arguably better at other sports. All-state in baseball, a state championship in basketball.
​
By his junior year he was one of the best linemen in the state. USC offered. UCLA. Utah.
​
He picked the school his dad had played for, committed early, and held it through a coaching change.
​
Then he left for two years and served a mission in Washington, D.C.
​
Somewhere in there came a crisis of faith, and a deeper conversion out the other side.
​
Then five seasons. 51 games, 41 starts, through coaching turnover and the move to the Big 12. A captain.
​
September 2024, in Waco, he broke the fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He'd broken the other one in high school, so he knew the surgery and the screw.
​
What he did not know was that an Apostle was in the stadium. Elder Ronald A. Rasband gave him a blessing.
​
He still won't describe it. "It was a pretty sacred experience."
​
He could have left after that season. His younger brother had just joined the line.
​
So he stayed a year longer, so they could be teammates for the first time in their lives.
​
He also built the thing he'd been turning over for years. A scripture podcast, made for teenagers.
​
He hadn't taken his own seriously at that age, and figured he might have if some BYU football players had made one.
​
He and a teammate pitched it at Big 12 media days. BYU Broadcasting said yes. It became one of their fastest growing shows.
​
Then came the draft. He trained in Atlanta. Scouts had him as a priority free agent. Teams were calling.
​
Then not one center came off the board the rest of the draft, the market flooded, and every team went dark.
​
Minicamps in Seattle and Las Vegas. The Raiders raised his reps. The front office decided otherwise.
​
So he came home, and Kalani Sitake asked him to help.
​
He is BYU's offensive line analyst now, working the part of the game he always loved most.
​
And the podcast he assumed he'd hand off to someone else? He is still recording it every week.
​
Connor Pay.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

text:
I can name 3 things. Enjoy your reading and have a great weekend, everybody! 
1. He made the border a real border again. In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.  2. He reversed mass migration. America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”   Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.  3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens. Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.  Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.  4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years. According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.  This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.  Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle  5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better. The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.  Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.  6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one. In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.  Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.  7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments. That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.   No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.  8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan. Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.  9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade. Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.  10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America. Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.  Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.  11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year. For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.  Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.  Trump Made Elections Matter Again  12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches. In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.  Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.  Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.  13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse. In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.   In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.  14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government. USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.  Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?  15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years. From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.  What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”  16. He expelled DEI from the federal government. Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.  He Defended Faith and Family  17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform. In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.  Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.  He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.  No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.  18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy. The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.  Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.  19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts. As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.  That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.  20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination. Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.  He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First  21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent. For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.  Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.  22. He drove China out of the Caribbean. China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.  Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.  23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months. In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.  24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population. Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.  Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.  25. text:
DO YOU REMEMBER THE THOUSANDS OF VIDEOS THAT STARTED APPEARING DURING THE FIFA WORLD CUP?

People from all over the world came to America - many for the FIRST TIME.

And something fascinating happened.

For years, many of them had built their picture of America from television, social media, political commentary and international news coverage.

The picture they had been given was something like this:

• Americans are RACIST.

• Americans don't like foreigners.

• Americans are rude and arrogant.

• America is dangerously divided.

• You could get shot walking down the street.

• Americans are hostile toward immigrants and tourists.

• Everyone is fighting over politics.

• American patriotism means Americans don't accept outsiders.

• The country is basically one giant political battlefield.

Then they actually ARRIVED.

And thousands of social-media posts started telling a very different story.

People were saying:

• Americans are incredibly FRIENDLY.

• Complete strangers offered them help.

• Uber drivers gave them recommendations and advice.

• Locals invited visitors into their HOMES.

• People bought them food and drinks.

• Americans supported foreign teams alongside visiting fans.

• Customer service surprised them.

• Southern and Texas hospitality became a massive talking point.

• People who arrived nervous said they actually felt SAFE.

• Some openly admitted that America was NOTHING like what they expected.

One British visitor literally said:

"We owe America a huge apology."

Another visitor described American hospitality as making you feel at HOME almost immediately.

That fascinates me.

Because something very similar is happening with what I'm trying to do for PAPUA NEW GUINEA.

Ask the average American what they know about PNG and chances are they have heard some combination of:

Dangerous.

Tribal fighting.

Crime.

Underdeveloped.

Cannibals.

Remote jungle.

No infrastructure.

Not somewhere tourists should go.

And unlike America, Papua New Guinea doesn't have a FIFA WORLD CUP bringing hundreds of thousands of foreigners through our doors at once.

I don't have a massive international tourism budget.

HausLink doesn't have millions of dollars to run global advertising campaigns.

There is no major international event happening here anytime soon that will suddenly put PNG in front of the world.

So I'm doing it the hard way.

ORGANICALLY.

One post.

One video.

One destination.

One tour operator.

One resort.

One traveller.

One American at a time.

My job right now isn't to pretend Papua New Guinea doesn't have problems.

WE DO.

My job is to show people that our problems are not the entirety of our country.

There is another PNG that millions of people around the world have NEVER BEEN SHOWN.

The people.

The hospitality.

The villages.

The islands.

The mountains.

The reefs.

The cultures.

The 800+ languages.

The stories.

The adventure.

And eventually I want Americans to arrive here carrying one perception of Papua New Guinea...

...and fly home telling their friends:

"PNG was NOTHING like I thought it would be."

That is what I'm building through HausLink.

No giant budget.

No World Cup.

No massive tourism machine behind me.

Just relentless organic work to change the perception of an entire country.

And if I have to convince people ONE TRAVELLER AT A TIME, that's exactly what I'm going to do. 🇵🇬🇺🇸

The SAVE America Act, sponsored in the Senate by Sen. Mike Lee (R-UT) and in the House by Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX), passed the House by a narrow 218–213 vote. The bill would require documentary proof of citizenship at voter registration and a photo ID at the polls. Sen. Schumer and Senate Democrats have characterized the measure as an effort to disenfranchise voters.

The push comes after Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin cited a preliminary DHS review identifying approximately 278,000 potential non-citizens on voter rolls across California, New Jersey, Nevada, and Pennsylvania — a figure the White House says is an undercount. Experts note such preliminary numbers are typically reduced significantly after full vetting, and a USCIS review found only 0.03% of records flagged as possible non-citizens merited further review.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune has warned the SAVE Act's fate will become a defining campaign issue this fall. Congress is also weighing a scaled-back reconciliation version that would offer states $10 billion in federal incentives to voluntarily adopt voter ID and proof-of-citizenship requirements.
